answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock. Consider a beacon as the anchor of the cost.
